samples.summary: The new `getStore()` proxy only guards `setPageSetup`; every other DocStore mutator still passes through unguarded, so read-only is still bypassable via `getStore()`
samples.evidence: `guardedStore`'s `get` trap (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2899-2909) special-cases only `'setPageSetup'` and binds every other member straight to the real `docStore`. `DocStore` exposes ~30 other writes — `setDocument`, `replaceDocument`, `updateBlock`, `insertBlock`, `deleteBlock`, `applyStyle`/`applyStyles`, `applyBlockStyle`, `setDocStyles`, `undo`/`redo`, table ops (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:15-146). The read-only neutering at the API boundary (editor.ts:3959-3981) blanks `applyStyle`, `undo`, `setDocStyles`, `paste`, etc., but a viewer holding `api` can call `editor.getStore().applyStyle(...)` or `editor.getStore().setDocument(...)` and, on `YorkieDocStore`, persist the write into the CRDT for every collaborator. Note `setDocument` also writes `root.pageSetup` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2872-2876), so it is a route around the new `assertUsablePageSetup` check as well. The new read-only test (editor-read-only.test.ts:325) asserts the handed-out store is safe, but only for one method. Fix belongs on the new proxy: guard the mutating surface, not one method.

samples.summary: `EditorAPI.getDoc()` hands out a `Doc` that writes straight through to the unguarded store — a second door beside the one this delta closed

samples.summary: The proxy's `set` trap is not the only way to overwrite `setPageSetup`; `Object.defineProperty` (what `vi.spyOn` uses) is not trapped and reaches the target
samples.evidence: The `set` trap at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2911-2914 refuses `setPageSetup` assignment, but there is no `defineProperty` trap, so `Object.defineProperty(editor.getStore(), 'setPageSetup', { value: fn })` — exactly what `vi.spyOn(store,'setPageSetup')` does — forwards to the real store and installs an own property that the `get` trap's `prop === 'setPageSetup'` branch would then still shadow (guard survives for reads) while the *underlying* store is permanently rewritten for every other holder, including `writePageSetup` at editor.ts:2086. Also note the `set` trap returning `false` throws a TypeError in strict-mode ESM rather than failing silently; no current caller assigns it (grep for `getStore().<x> =` and `spyOn(...getStore` found none), so this is forward-looking.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The new `guardedStore` proxy (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2899-2915) intercepts only `'setPageSetup'` (line 2901); all other members are `Reflect.get` + `.bind(target)`-ed straight onto the live `docStore` (2902-2908). The read-only neutering list at editor.ts:3959-3981 only rewrites methods on `api` and does not include `getStore`, which returns the proxy (editor.ts:2920). `DocStore` exposes ~30 other mutators (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:15,21,23-26,34,50-51,72-74,76-97,116,57-69,146) reachable unguarded through that pass-through. Frontend hands a read-only editor the same writable store (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:327), and on `YorkieDocStore` `setDocument` writes `root.pageSetup` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2872-2878, 2897-2899), so it is also a route around the new `assertUsablePageSetup` validation (editor.ts:2896). The only counter-signal is a comment claiming read-only is a client-side convenience (editor.ts:3956-3958), which is not an enforced guard and is contradicted by the diff's own `if (readOnly) return;` (editor.ts:2895). getStore() is a public, externally consumed surface (docs-find-bar.tsx:56, docs-export-button.tsx:53, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:470, harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386), so the bypass path is reachable. Squarely in the blast-radius lane: a new guard with sibling entry points, defined outside the diff, reaching the same protected mutation.

verdict.reason: The finding is factually accurate. `editor.ts:1039` constructs `new Doc(docStore)` over the raw store, and `editor.ts:2919` (`getDoc: () => doc`) hands that model out as public `EditorAPI` (declared `editor.ts:53`). `Doc` holds `private store: DocStore` (document.ts:98) and delegates mutations unguarded: `insertText` (document.ts:261), `deleteText` (document.ts:278), `applyBlockStyle` (document.ts:600), `deleteBlock` (document.ts:628), `insertBlockAfter` (document.ts:664, 770). The read-only neutering at editor.ts:3959-3981 only replaces methods on the `api` object and does not include `getDoc`, and the new `guardedStore` proxy (editor.ts:2899-2915) is only returned by `getStore()`, so neither covers this path. The bypass is live from the frontend: docs-find-bar.tsx:55 builds `FindReplaceState(editor.getDoc(), ...)` and find-replace.ts:79-83 calls `doc.deleteText`/`doc.insertText`, while docs-view.tsx:599-604 renders the find bar without any readOnly gate. No guard elsewhere makes it unreachable; the "by design" note at editor-read-only.test.ts:286-289 is prose, not enforcement. Under the blast-radius rubric this is a reachable bypass of a guard the diff added/relies on, i.e. major. Narrow caveat: the specific new `setPageSetup` guard is NOT reachable through `Doc` (no pageSetup delegation in document.ts), but the read-only mutation guard as a whole is.

finding.summary: `EditorAPI.getStore()` exposes `DocStore.setPageSetup`, which bypasses both `assertUsablePageSetup` and the read-only neutering of `setPageSetup`
finding.evidence: `getStore: () => docStore` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2866) is public on `EditorAPI` (interface at editor.ts:55) and is already used from the frontend (`docs-export-button.tsx:53` calls `editor.getStore().getDocument()`). `DocStore.setPageSetup` (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:28; `MemDocStore` at packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:98, `YorkieDocStore` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2710) performs no validation, takes no snapshot, and triggers no `doc.refresh()`/relayout/render. So `editor.getStore().setPageSetup(bad)` reaches the CRDT with hostile geometry, with no undo entry and a stale layout — and it still does so on a read-only mount, where `initialize()` only replaces the `api.setPageSetup` entry (editor.ts:3915). No in-tree caller does this today, which is why this is a latent bypass rather than a live bug; the design doc that asserts the opposite is `docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md:350` ("there is no second way to write a page setup").

verdict.reason: The claimed bypass does not exist in this tree. `getStore` does not return the raw `docStore`: at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2920 it returns `guardedStore`, a Proxy over `docStore` (editor.ts:2899-2915) whose `get` trap intercepts `setPageSetup` and returns `guardedSetPageSetup` (editor.ts:2888-2898), which applies exactly the two protections the finding says are bypassed: `if (readOnly) return;` (editor.ts:2895) and `assertUsablePageSetup(setup)` (editor.ts:2896) before writing `resolvePageSetup(setup)` to the store. The proxy's `set` trap also refuses assignment over `setPageSetup` (editor.ts:2912), closing the obvious way around the wrapper, and every other member is delegated bound to the real store with memoized identity (editor.ts:2902-2908), so the export-button read path (`editor.getStore().getDocument()`) still works. The reviewer's quoted evidence line `getStore: () => docStore` (claimed at editor.ts:2866) is not present; line 2866 is a comment describing precisely this guard. No other accessor hands out the raw store (only internal uses at editor.ts:2724 and 3114). Both behaviours are covered by existing tests: packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts:338 asserts `editor.getStore().setPageSetup(closed)` throws RangeError and leaves `pageSetup` unwritten, and packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:331-336 asserts a read-only mount's `getStore().setPageSetup(...)` writes nothing. The residual sub-claim (no snapshot/`doc.refresh()`/relayout on the store-level write) is an explicit, documented property of store-level writes shared by every other `getStore()` mutation (editor.ts:2893-2894) and is logic inside the new code, i.e. the correctness lens's lane, not a bypassing call site — it does not make this a blocking blast-radius defect.
